When three friends sold their video games, Ryan, the first of the three friends, received $50 more than Jason from his sales. Jason received 30% more money than Zachary from selling his video games. If Zachary sold 40 games at $5 each, calculate the total amount of money the three friends received together from the sale of the video games.

Given:
- Zachary sold 40 games at $5 each.
- Jason received 30% more money than Zachary.
- Ryan received $50 more than Jason.

First, calculate Zachary's total earnings:
\[ 40 \text{ games} \times \$5 \text{ per game} = \$200 \]

Next, calculate Jason's earnings. Jason received 30% more than Zachary:
\[ 30\% \text{ of } \$200 = 0.30 \times 200 = \$60 \]
\[ \text{Jason's total} = \$200 + \$60 = \$260 \]

Now, calculate Ryan's earnings. Ryan received $50 more than Jason:
\[ \text{Ryan's total} = \$260 + \$50 = \$310 \]

Finally, add up the total earnings of all three friends:
\[ \text{Total} = \$200 + \$260 + \$310 = \$770 \]

FINAL: 770
